thread:
Maria Chen: ran a long nsys capture on the inference cluster, seeing periodic H2D async memcpy stalls that line up with KV prefetch windows. timeline shows big memcpy_async (host->device) spikes at ~1.2s and ~2.6s causing tail latency p99 jumps. trace id trace-1790001111 and I uploaded the .nsys to s3.

Alex J: can you paste the exact nsys command and a short snippet of the timeline events? are those cudaMemcpyAsync from pageable host memory?

Maria Chen: command I used:```nsys profile -o run1790001111 --trace=cuda --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --duration=180 ./perf_test --model=llm_xl --batch=1 --seq=1024 --kv-prefetch=1```timeline note: several entries labeled "cudaMemcpyAsync H2D (pageable)" with wait stalls labeled "host pageable pin" and CPU thread blocking ~2-6ms each. aggregate H2D transfer time spikes correlate with kv_prefetch_start events.

Kyle S: that sounds like transient pageable->pinned conversion stalls. If the allocator hands back host pointers that are pageable, cuda will pin them on demand which blocks the CPU and creates these stalls. NVLink+P2P helps only if peer pointers are device memory and peer access is enabled. If we fall back to PCIe for peer copies or use host pageable memory, bandwidth/tails tank.

Ram Patel: confirm. last month we hit similar with the prefetcher: it used a host-buffer for gathering keys and then cuMemcpyPeerAsync to push shards, but because the buffer was not pinned we saw cudaHostRegister overheads. Proposed: allocator.pin_for_dma(ptr, size) that uses cudaHostRegister/cudaHostAlloc for prefetch buffers, and expose a policy flag prefetch.use_pinned=true.

Alex J: I also noticed kernel selection churn after the recent matmul-path change: for short sequences we sometimes pick the matmul-cuBLAS path which increases intermediate host copies for KV shard assembly. might be interaction between kernel selection + batching heuristic causing more host-device shuttle.

Maria Chen: yep, performance regression timeline aligns with that kernel selection change 3 days ago. p99 latency up ~15-20% on canary. Repro steps I ran: B=1, seq=256, kv_prefetch=1, run 10 warmups, then collect 200 samples. nsys shows repeated host->device memcpy_async with "pageable" annotation.

perf-bot: nsys trace archived at s3://redwood-traces/1790001111.nsys and perf dashboard entry created: /perf/dash/1790001111 (auto-tag: kv-prefetch, h2d-stall)

Kyle S: short-term mitigation: change batching heuristic to skip aggressive prefetch when batch_size<=2 or seq_len<=512. Also change allocator to allocate prefetch buffers with cudaHostAlloc (pinned) when prefetch.enabled. That should eliminate the on-demand pinning penalty.

Ram Patel: agree. I'll draft an allocator patch that adds Alloc::alloc_dma(size, hint) -> calls cudaHostAlloc(..., cudaHostAllocPortable) for nodes where we expect peer copies. We'll need unit test that asserts copy type shows as "pinned" in nsys.

Alex J: can we also tweak kernel selector to avoid matmul-cuBLAS path for short sequences until we validate no extra host copies are introduced? add a feature-flagged rollout.

Maria Chen: plan: 1) push allocator pin_for_prefetch behind config flag, 2) add batching heuristic guard, 3) roll canary 50% at 13:00 PT with both changes + kernel-selector rollback for short seqs. I'll run a sanity nsys capture after canary and post results. cc @Ram for review.

Ram Patel: :thumbsup: I'll add a perf CI job for a peercopy-heavy scenario and add a small integration test to assert no on-demand host pin events.

Kyle S: follow-up note: if NVLink saturation is the root cause we should also add a bandwidth-slowdown detector in runtime that falls back to smaller prefetch windows or serializes peer copies to avoid peak contention. but first fix the pageable pinning.

Maria Chen: sounds good — thanks all. I'll paste the canary trace once uploaded and tag this thread.
